name: Idris
title: A man of truth, raised to a high station
sentTo: The descendants of Adam (AS) before or after Nuh (AS); the Quran does not say
era: Very early. Most scholars place him between Adam and Nuh (AS); the Quran and Sunnah give no date.

places.name: Not known. The Quran does not say where Idris lived.

summary: A Prophet praised in the Quran as a man of truth, patient and righteous, whom Allah raised to a high station. Very little about his life is known for certain, and the Quran mentions him only twice.
notes: Most scholars say Idris lived between Adam and Nuh (AS). Many identify him with Enoch (Akhnukh) of the Bible; this comes from historians and the People of the Book, not from the Quran or Sunnah.
'We raised him to a high station' (19:57): many scholars say it means a high rank of honour and prophethood; others say he was raised to one of the heavens.
Popular reports that he was the first to write with a pen, to sew clothes or to study the stars come from later sources, not from the Quran or authentic hadith.

chapters.title: A man of truth
paragraphs: The Quran asks us to remember Idris (AS). Allah describes him as a man of truth and a Prophet, and says: “We raised him to a high station.”
Allah also names him with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl (AS) as being among the patient, and says that He admitted them into His mercy, for they were among the righteous.

That is almost all that we know about Idris for certain. The Quran gives us his qualities rather than his story: truthfulness, patience and righteousness. These are the qualities that raise a person in Allah's sight.
kidsParagraphs: Idris was a Prophet who always told the truth.
Allah says he was patient and good, and raised him to a high place. We can be truthful and patient like him!

blocks.text: Some books say Idris was the first to write with a pen and to sew clothes, or describe how he was taken up to heaven by an angel.

lessons: Truthfulness is one of the greatest qualities of the Prophets.
Patience brings a person into Allah's mercy.
What matters most about a person is their character, not how much is known about them.

options: Raised him to a high station

quiz.question: With which two Prophets is Idris named as one of the patient?

chapters.title: Greeting the Prophet ﷺ in the heavens
paragraphs: On the night of the Mi'raj, when the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was taken up through the heavens, he met several of the earlier Prophets. One of them was Idris.
Idris welcomed him with the words: “Welcome, righteous Prophet and righteous brother.” The Prophets greeted one another as brothers, because their message was one: to worship Allah alone.
kidsParagraphs: On the night of the Mi'raj, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ met Idris in the heavens.
Idris said: “Welcome, righteous Prophet and righteous brother!” All the Prophets are like brothers.

blocks.narrator: Anas ibn Malik, from Abu Dharr
blocks.translation: …Anas said: “When Jibril passed with the Prophet ﷺ by Idris, he said: ‘Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous brother.’ The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Who is this?’ Jibril said: ‘This is Idris.’”
blocks.match: فلما مر جبريل بادريس قال مرحبا بالنبي الصالح والاخ الصالح

lessons: All the Prophets are brothers with one message.
Welcoming others warmly is the way of the Prophets.
The Mi'raj showed the honour Allah gave to His Prophets.

quiz.question: When did the Prophet ﷺ meet Idris?
options: On the night of the Mi'raj
